_doc: Comic events (docs/ue58/HUMOR_EVENTOS_COMICOS.md), read by UMareComicEvents. One at a time; each has its own cooldown in game minutes and there is a global gap between any two. Every check_seconds the manager rolls 'odds' for each due event (hours = game hours it may happen). A pedestrian near the player (min..max cm) stops, faces the player and calls; E opens a short exchange: the line ('asks', in order when sequence is true, so the stories grow), the player's replies and the matching reactions. Ignored for wait_seconds, it ends by itself. max_y: only when the player is on the beach side (world y below it), facing the sea. Nothing touches money, stock or orders. kind 'gull' (HUM-001): a seagull swoops on a customer eating one of 'foods', takes a bit and flies off; the customer's line shows as a notice. _en fields are the English text for the localization pass. kind "umbrella" (HUM-004): the wind knocks over the beach umbrella built on pole_mesh (its parts share the pole's XY) and rolls it 'distance' cm along the beach onto open sand; E puts it back, otherwise it is put back unseen. kind "clumsy" (HUM-006): the attendant ('role') almost drops what it carries; odds fall with the worker level. prop (talk events): a mesh in the caller's hand while calling (HUM-002's phone).

events.name: Gaivota ladra de batatas
events.speaker: Cliente
asks: Ei! A gaivota levou minha batata!
Aquela gaivota... levou um pedaço e nem pediu licença!
Volta aqui, sua ladra! Essa era a mais crocante!
asks_en: Hey! The seagull took my fries!
That seagull... grabbed a piece without even asking!
Come back here, you thief! That was the crunchiest one!
reactions: Na próxima eu como mais rápido do que ela.
reactions_en: Next time I'll eat faster than it does.

events.name: Turista perdido
events.speaker: Turista perdido
asks: Com licença! Você sabe onde fica a praia? Me disseram que era por aqui.
Oi, moço! Esse mar todo aí... é a praia ou ainda falta andar?
Desculpa incomodar: qual é o caminho mais rápido pra areia? Estou procurando faz meia hora.
asks_en: Excuse me! Do you know where the beach is? They told me it was around here.
Hi! All this sea here... is that the beach, or do I still have to walk?
Sorry to bother you: what's the quickest way to the sand? I've been looking for half an hour.
replies_en: Follow the sound of the waves.
reactions: Atrás de mim? ... Ah. AH. Aquele azul enorme. Eu achei que era o céu caindo no chão. Obrigado!
Que ideia boa! Eu estava seguindo o barulho do caminhão de sorvete. Valeu!
reactions_en: Behind me? ... Oh. OH. That huge blue thing. I thought it was the sky lying down. Thanks!
Great idea! I was following the ice-cream truck jingle. Thanks!

events.name: Seu Arnaldo reclama
events.speaker: Seu Arnaldo
asks: Essa água de coco está muito natural. Vocês não têm uma mais industrializada?
O sol hoje está forte demais. Na minha época o sol era mais educado.
Essa brisa do mar fica bagunçando meu cabelo. Dá pra desligar um pouquinho?
A areia daqui é fina demais, entra em tudo. Não tem uma areia mais... grossa?
O mar está fazendo barulho de novo. Ninguém fala nada pra ele?
asks_en: This coconut water is far too natural. Don't you have a more processed one?
The sun is too strong today. In my day the sun had better manners.
This sea breeze keeps messing up my hair. Could you turn it down a little?
The sand here is too fine, it gets everywhere. Don't you have a... chunkier sand?
The sea is making noise again. Doesn't anybody say anything to it?
replies: Vou ver o que posso fazer, Seu Arnaldo.
replies_en: I'll see what I can do, Mr. Arnaldo.
That's the charm of the beach!
reactions: Hmpf. Pelo menos aqui alguém me escuta. Volto amanhã pra reclamar de novo.
Charme... sei. Mas tudo bem, ainda é o melhor quiosque da praia. Não conte pra ninguém que eu disse isso.
reactions_en: Hmph. At least somebody listens to me here. I'll be back tomorrow to complain again.
Charm... sure. But fine, it's still the best kiosk on the beach. Don't tell anyone I said that.

events.name: Pescador e o peixe
events.speaker: Seu Bené, pescador
asks: Ontem pesquei um robalo de uns dois quilos. Bonito que só ele!
Lembra do robalo? Pensei melhor: tinha uns cinco quilos. Quase me puxou do barco.
Aquele robalo... na verdade era uma garoupa de vinte quilos. Precisei de dois amigos pra segurar.
A garoupa, sabe? Eram trinta quilos e ela falava. Pediu pra eu soltar e eu soltei, por educação.
O peixe daquele dia? Era do tamanho da jangada. Hoje ele manda lembranças.
asks_en: Yesterday I caught a two-kilo snook. A real beauty!
Remember the snook? Thinking it over, it was about five kilos. Nearly pulled me off the boat.
That snook... it was actually a twenty-kilo grouper. Took two friends to hold it.
The grouper, you know? Thirty kilos, and it talked. Asked me to let it go, so I did, out of politeness.
The fish from that day? As big as the jangada. It sends its regards today.
replies: Da última vez ele era menor...
reactions: Pois é! Um dia te levo no barco e você vê com os próprios olhos.
Menor? Impossível. Peixe de história só cresce, nunca diminui.
reactions_en: Right? One day I'll take you on the boat and you'll see it with your own eyes.
Smaller? Impossible. Story fish only grow, they never shrink.

events.name: Influenciador exigente
events.speaker: Influencer
asks: Oi! Essa luz não está boa pro meu feed... Vocês têm uma mesa com vista pro mar?
Rapidinho: em qual ângulo o quiosque fica mais bonito? Meus seguidores são exigentes.
Qual mesa tem a melhor luz? Minha câmera só gosta de pôr do sol, e ainda é meio-dia.
asks_en: Hi! This light isn't working for my feed... Do you have a table with a sea view?
Quick one: from which angle does the kiosk look best? My followers are picky.
Which table has the best light? My camera only likes sunsets, and it's barely noon.
replies: As mesas da frente dão para o mar.
Aqui toda hora é hora dourada.
replies_en: The front tables face the sea.
Here every hour is golden hour.
reactions: Perfeito! Vou marcar o quiosque nos stories. #MaréAlta
Hora dourada... vou usar isso de legenda. Obrigado, você é um talento!
reactions_en: Perfect! I'll tag the kiosk in my stories. #MareAlta
Golden hour... I'm using that as a caption. Thanks, you're a natural!

events.name: Guarda-sol levado pelo vento
events.speaker: Banhista
asks: Ei! Volta aqui, guarda-sol!
Meu guarda-sol saiu passeando sozinho!
Alguém segura esse guarda-sol fujão!
asks_en: Hey! Come back here, umbrella!
My umbrella went for a walk on its own!
Somebody grab that runaway umbrella!

events.name: Atendente atrapalhado
events.speaker: Atendente
asks: Opa, opa, opa... ufa! Tudo inteiro.
Quase! Essa bandeja tem vida própria.
Ninguém viu isso, né? Tá tudo certo aqui!
asks_en: Whoa, whoa, whoa... phew! All in one piece.
Close one! This tray has a mind of its own.
Nobody saw that, right? Everything's fine here!
